personnel: Lee Renacre James Chapman Doran Walker

title: Electric Music For The Mind And Body
label: Vanguard
personnel: Country Joe McDonald - lead vocals, rhythm guitar. Barry " The Fish" Melton - lead guitar, vocals
Bruce Barthol - bass, harmonica. Gary "Chicken" Hirsh - drums
about: First album by the Berkeley band Country Joe and the Fish, released on Vanguard. Combining psychedelic rock, organ-driven jams and political satire, it became a key document of the San Francisco Bay Area sound of the late 1960s.

title: Ella Fitzgerald Sings The Gershwin Song Book Vol. 1
label: Verve Records

tracks.t: Nice Work If You Can Get It
Let's Call The Whole Thing Off

about: Large Verve project in which Ella Fitzgerald interprets dozens of songs by George and Ira Gershwin, arranged and conducted by Nelson Riddle. Originally spread over several LPs, it was part of her celebrated Song Book series dedicated to major American popular songwriters.

title: In Through The Out Door
label: Classic Records
personnel: John Bonham – drums, percussion John Paul Jones – bass guitar, keyboards Jimmy Page – guitars, gizmotron Robert Plant – lead vocals
about: The last Led Zeppelin studio album issued before drummer John Bonham's death in 1980. Recorded in Stockholm, it gives a larger role to John Paul Jones's keyboards, and it reached number one in both the United Kingdom and the United States.

title: Crosby, Stills & Nash
label: Atlantic Records
personnel: David Crosby – vocals, guitars Stephen Stills – vocals, guitars, bass, keyboards, percussion Graham Nash – vocals, guitars
about: Debut record by the trio of David Crosby, Stephen Stills and Graham Nash, issued by Atlantic. Known for its close vocal harmonies and songs such as Suite: Judy Blue Eyes and Marrakesh Express, it was a major commercial success and helped define folk rock at the end of the decade.

title: Wheels Of Fire
label: ATCO Records
personnel: Jack Bruce – vocals, bass , cello, harmonica, calliope, acoustic guitar, recorder Ginger Baker – drums, percussion, bells, glockenspiel, timpani, vocals Eric Clapton – guitar, vocals Felix Pappalardi – viola, bells, organ, trumpet, tonette

tracks.t: Sitting On Top Of The World

about: Double album by Cream pairing one disc of studio recordings with one disc of concert performances, much of it captured at the Fillmore in San Francisco. It includes White Room and a long live Crossroads, and it topped the US chart.

title: Revolver
label: Parlophone
personnel: John Lennon – vocals, guitar, organ, Mellotron, harmonium
Paul McCartney – vocals, guitar, piano, clavichord
George Harrison – vocals; guitar, sitar, tambura
Ringo Starr – drums; tambourine, maracas, cowbell, shaker
about: Beatles album that pushed studio experimentation further, using tape loops, reversed sounds and Indian instrumentation. Songs range from Eleanor Rigby to Tomorrow Never Knows, and it is frequently cited among the most influential albums in popular music.

title: Dig Your Own Hole
label: Freestyle Dust
personnel: Tom Rowlands – production Ed Simons – production

tracks.t: Get Up On It Like This

about: Second album by the English electronic duo The Chemical Brothers, featuring Block Rockin' Beats and Setting Sun with Noel Gallagher on vocals. It topped the UK chart and became a defining big beat record of the late 1990s.

title: Who's Next
label: MCA Records
personnel: Roger Daltrey – vocals John Entwistle – bass, brass, vocals, piano Keith Moon – drums, percussion Pete Townshend – guitar, VCS 3, organ, ARP synthesizer, vocals, piano
about: Album built from songs salvaged from Pete Townshend's abandoned Lifehouse project. Noted for its synthesizer textures on Baba O'Riley and Won't Get Fooled Again, it reached number one in the UK and is often named among the greatest rock albums.

title: Wonderful Sarah
label: Mercury Records
about: Mercury LP (MG 20219) by jazz and pop singer Sarah Vaughan, gathering twelve songs such as Mr. Wonderful, Whatever Lola Wants and Old Devil Moon. Much of the material reflects the pop-oriented recordings she made for the label in the mid-1950s.

title: Brubeck On Campus
label: Columbia
personnel: Dave Brubeck – piano Paul Desmond – alto saxophone Bob Bates – double bass Joe Dodge – drums

tracks.t: I'm Afraid The Masquerade Is Over

about: Two-record Columbia set reissuing college concert performances by the Dave Brubeck Quartet with Paul Desmond, recorded in the early 1950s. Produced for reissue by Teo Macero, it includes pieces such as Balcony Rock, Le Souk and The Song Is You.

title: Thr!!!er
label: Warp Records
personnel: Rafael Cohen – vocals, guitars, keyboards Nic Offer – vocals, keyboards
Mario Andreoni – guitar, keyboards Allan Wilson – saxophone, keyboards, percussion, background vocals Daniel Gorman – keyboards, background vocals
about: Fifth album by the dance-punk band !!!, released on Warp and produced with Jim Eno of Spoon. It leans toward tighter disco and funk song structures and includes the single One Girl / One Boy.

title: All You Writers / Gonna Guetta Stomp
label: Warp Records
about: Single by the dance-punk band !!! combining two songs from their 2015 album As If, issued on Warp ahead of and around the album's release.

title: Shake The Shudder
label: Warp Records
personnel: Rafael Cohen – vocals, guitars, keyboards Nic Offer – vocals, keyboards
Mario Andreoni – guitar, keyboards Allan Wilson – saxophone, keyboards, percussion, background vocals Daniel Gorman – keyboards, background vocals
about: Seventh album by !!!, released on Warp, continuing the group's mix of dance-punk, house and disco. It features several guest vocalists, including Lea Lea, and singles such as The One 2.

title: Something Special
label: De-Lite Records
personnel: Charles Smith – Lead guitar Ronald Bell – Saxophone, keyboards
George Brown – Drums. James "J.T." Taylor – vocals
Clifford Adams, Michael Ray, Robert Mickens – Trumpet

tracks.t: Take My Heart (You Can Have It If You Want It)

about: Kool & the Gang album produced with Eumir Deodato during the group's commercial peak with singer James J.T. Taylor. It yielded hits including Get Down On It, Take My Heart and Steppin' Out, and it reached the top of the US R&B album chart.

title: What's Going On
label: Tamla

tracks.t: Inner City Blues (Make Me Wanna Holler)

about: Song cycle in which Marvin Gaye addresses war, poverty, drug abuse and environmental damage from the perspective of a returning Vietnam veteran. Self-produced for Tamla against early label resistance, it became a commercial success and is widely ranked among the greatest albums ever made.

title: Exotic Percussion
label: Liberty Records

tracks.t: Softly, As In A Morning Sunrise
The Girl Friend Of The Whirling Dervish

about: Martin Denny album built around unusual percussion, combining jazz instrumentation with instruments such as Japanese shamisen and Burmese gongs. It is part of his exotica catalogue for Liberty and was later reissued on vinyl by Jackpot Records.

title: To The 5 Boroughs
label: Capitol Records
personnel: Michael "Mike D" Diamond - vocals, drums. Adam "MCA" Yauch - vocals, bass. Adam "Ad-Rock" Horovitz - vocals, guitar, programming
about: Beastie Boys album produced by the group themselves, drawing on old-school hip hop and serving as a tribute to New York City after the September 11 attacks. It debuted at number one in the US and includes the single Ch-Check It Out.

title: Exotica
label: Liberty Records
personnel: Martin Denny – piano, arrangements Arthur Lyman – vibes, xylophone, percussion
Augie Colon – bongos, congas, Latin effects, bird calls Harold Chang – drums, percussion
about: First album by pianist Martin Denny, featuring a cover of Les Baxter's Quiet Village with bird calls and Polynesian percussion. Its success, especially after a stereo version, gave the exotica genre its name and made Denny its leading figure.

title: Wallop
label: Warp Records
personnel: Rafael Cohen – vocals, guitar, bass, keyboards Mario Andreoni – guitar, bass, keyboards Dan Gorman – keyboards, trumpet
about: Eighth album by !!!, released on Warp, which broadens the band's dance-punk sound with elements of pop, house and electro. Singles included Off the Grid and Serbia Drums.

title: Gershwin '79
label: Parachute Records

tracks.t: Medley: The Man I Love / Embraceable You
Medley: I Got Rhythm / Fascinating Rhythm

about: Disco album by a one-off studio ensemble that recasts George and Ira Gershwin standards, including Rhapsody in Blue and I Got Rhythm, as extended dance medleys. Produced by drummer Ross Salomone, it features Los Angeles session players such as Jerry Hey.

title: Rose In The Dark
label: Forever Living Originals
about: The first full-length album by London singer Cleo Sol, issued on Forever Living Originals and produced by her husband Inflo. Its eleven songs blend soul and gospel-tinged R&B, and several critics placed it on their lists of the best records of 2020.

title: O.S.T.
label: Piecelock 70
personnel: Thes One (Christopher Portugal) Double K (Michael Turner)
about: The third album by Los Angeles hip hop duo People Under the Stairs, released on Om Records. Built partly from records the pair bought on a European tour, it marked their first use of live instruments and includes Acid Raindrops, which became a fan favorite.

title: Demon Days
label: Not On Label (Gorillaz)
personnel: Damon Albarn – vocals, keyboards, acoustic guitar, synthesizers, melodica Danger Mouse – percussion, drum programming, sampled loops Jason Cox – bass guitar, additional guitars, drums, drum programming James Dring – drums, drum programming Cass Browne – drums

tracks.t: Every Planet We Reach Is Dead
Fire Coming Out Of The Monkey's Head

about: Gorillaz's second album, made mainly with producer Danger Mouse and released by Parlophone and Virgin. It reached number one in the UK, sold roughly eight million copies worldwide, and spawned singles such as Feel Good Inc., which earned a Grammy award.

title: Black Pumas
label: ATO Records
personnel: Adrian Quesada – guitar, producer, engineering, mixing

tracks.t: Ain't No Love In The Heart Of The City

about: The self-titled first album by Austin psychedelic soul duo Black Pumas, released by ATO Records and produced by Adrian Quesada with Jon Kaplan. A deluxe version was nominated for Album of the Year at the Grammys, and the single Colors also drew major nominations.

title: Christmas Songs
label: Epitaph
personnel: Greg Graffin – lead vocals Brett Gurewitz – guitar, backing vocals Brian Baker – lead guitar Jay Bentley – bass, backing vocals Brooks Wackerman – drums

tracks.t: Angels We Have Heard On High

about: A short holiday release from punk band Bad Religion on Epitaph, featuring punk arrangements of traditional carols plus a remix of American Jesus. Part of the proceeds went to a support network for survivors of clergy abuse, and it reached the US holiday album chart.

title: Summertime: Willie Nelson Sings Gershwin
label: Legacy

tracks.t: Lets Call The Whole Thing Off
They Can't Take That Away From Me

about: Willie Nelson recorded these George and Ira Gershwin standards after receiving the Library of Congress Gershwin Prize. Produced by Buddy Cannon and Matt Rollings, it features duets with Cyndi Lauper and Sheryl Crow and won the Grammy for Best Traditional Pop Vocal Album.

tracks.t: On Your WAy To The Ground

title: Takes Off
label: RCA Records
personnel: Marty Balin – vocals, rhythm guitar Signe Toly Anderson – vocals, percussion Jorma Kaukonen – lead guitar Paul Kantner – rhythm guitar, vocals Jack Casady – bass guitar
about: The first album by San Francisco band Jefferson Airplane, released on RCA Victor before Grace Slick joined, with Signe Toly Anderson singing. RCA pushed for lyric edits on some songs, so early pressings differ, and initial sales were modest.

title: Butts Band
label: Blue Thumb Records
personnel: Jess Roden – vocals, rhythm guitar Robby Krieger – lead guitar (ex-Doors) Roy Davies – keyboards, synthesizers Phil Chen – bass, rhythm guitar John Densmore – drums (ex-Doors)
about: The first record by Butts Band, formed by former Doors members Robby Krieger and John Densmore with singer Jess Roden. Produced by Bruce Botnick for Blue Thumb, it offers rock with reggae touches; the band changed lineup entirely before its second album.

title: Genius + Soul = Jazz
label: Impulse!

tracks.t: I'm Gonna Move To The Outskirts Of Town

about: An Impulse! album on which Ray Charles plays Hammond organ in front of big bands drawn from Count Basie players, with arrangements by Quincy Jones and Ralph Burns. It climbed to number four on the Billboard album chart and later entered the Grammy Hall of Fame.

title: Handful Of Soul
label: Smash Records

tracks.t: When A Man Loves A Woman

about: An all-instrumental James Brown album released on Smash Records, with Brown playing organ over a band arranged by saxophonist Nat Jones. It was recorded during 1966 in New York and Charlotte, and its version of Let's Go Get Stoned was issued as a single.

title: Some Girls
label: Rolling Stones Records
personnel: Mick Jagger – vocals, electric guitar, piano, percussion
Keith Richards – electric guitar, vocals, acoustic guitar, bass guitar, piano
Ronnie Wood – electric guitar, vocals, pedal steel, acoustic guitar, bass
Bill Wyman – bass , synthesiser Charlie Watts – drums

tracks.t: Just My Imagination (Running Away With Me)

about: The Rolling Stones recorded this album in Paris, the first with Ronnie Wood as a full member. It reflects punk and disco influences, topped the US chart, became their best-selling US album, and produced hits including Miss You and Beast of Burden.

title: Book Of Dreams
label: Edsel Records
personnel: Steve Miller – vocals, guitar, synthesizer, sitar, producer David Denny – guitar Greg Douglass – guitar, slide guitar
Byron Allred – piano, synthesizer Lonnie Turner – bass guitar
about: The Steve Miller Band's follow-up to Fly Like an Eagle, drawn largely from the same mid-1970s sessions in San Francisco. Released by Capitol, it reached number two in the US, went triple platinum, and included the singles Jet Airliner, Jungle Love and Swingtown.

title: The Score
label: Ruffhouse Records
personnel: Wyclef Jean – vocals, guitar, producer Lauryn Hill – vocals, producer, arranger Pras Michel – vocals, producer
John Forté – vocals, producer. Diamond D, DJ Red Alert, Omega, Pacewon, Rah Digga, Young Zee – vocals
about: The second and last album by the Fugees, issued by Ruffhouse and Columbia. Featuring Killing Me Softly and Ready or Not, it topped the US chart, sold around 22 million copies, and won the Grammy for Best Rap Album.

title: Band On The Run
label: Apple Records
personnel: Paul McCartney – vocals; bass, guitar; piano, keyboards; drums, percussion Linda McCartney – harmony and backing vocals; organ, keyboards
Denny Laine – vocals; acoustic and electric guitars; percussion
about: The third Wings album, recorded largely in Lagos, Nigeria, after two members quit, leaving Paul and Linda McCartney with Denny Laine. Driven by the hits Jet and the title track, it became a major seller in 1974 and entered the Grammy Hall of Fame.

title: Coming Home
label: Columbia
personnel: Austin Jenkins – electric guitar, acoustic guitar, bass
Jeff Dazey – saxophone, piano, baritone saxophone, tenor saxophone
about: Leon Bridges' first album, released on Columbia and produced by the Niles City Sound team in Fort Worth. Its retro soul style drew comparisons to 1960s records; it reached number six in the US, went platinum, and earned a Grammy nomination for Best R&B Album.

tracks.t: Back Road Roll With The Punches
Tommy Tutone What's It Gonna Do For You

title: The Live Mix Part 2
label: Stones Throw Records
personnel: Miles Tackett ("Musicman") - vocals, bass, cello, guitar
about: The second Live Mix release from Los Angeles funk ensemble Breakestra, led by Miles Tackett and issued by Stones Throw. The band plays a continuous run of classic funk and soul breaks on real instruments, and reviewers in Billboard and AllMusic responded positively.

title: H2O
label: RCA Records
personnel: Daryl Hall – vocals, guitar, keyboards, synthesizers John Oates – vocals, guitar, electric piano, Roland CR-78 drum machine G.E
Smith – lead guitar. Tom "T-Bone" Wolk – bass
Mickey Curry – drums. Charlie "Mr. Casual" DeChant – saxophone
about: The eleventh album from Daryl Hall and John Oates, recorded at Electric Lady Studios and released by RCA. It reached number three in the US, their best album chart placing, and contained Maneater, which held the top spot of the Hot 100 for four weeks.

title: Private Eyes
label: RCA Records
personnel: Daryl Hall – vocals, keyboards, synthesizers, mando-guitar, mandocello, mandolin, mandola, vibraphone, timbales, Roland CR-78 drum machine
John Oates – vocals, guitar, mando-guitar, keyboards
Smith, Ray Gomez, Jeff Southworth – guitar
Mickey Curry, Jerry Marotta, Chuck Burgi – drums
about: The tenth album by Daryl Hall and John Oates, self-produced with Neil Kernon for RCA. It gave the duo two US number one singles, the title song and I Can't Go for That (No Can Do), and reached the top five of the Billboard 200.

title: Afro Roots
label: Prestige Records
about: A double-LP reissue gathering two late-1950s Fantasy albums by Cuban percussionist Mongo Santamaria, Yambu and Mongo. The material leans toward traditional Afro-Cuban rhythms and early Latin jazz, and includes the first recording of his composition Afro Blue.

title: The Trinity Session
label: RCA Records
personnel: Margo Timmins – lead vocals Michael Timmins – guitar Alan Anton – bass Peter Timmins – drums

tracks.t: I'm So Lonesome I Could Cry

about: Cowboy Junkies cut this second album in one day inside a Toronto church, gathered around a single microphone. First issued in Canada and then globally by RCA, it mixes originals with slowed covers such as Sweet Jane and became their breakthrough.

title: Hot On The Tracks
label: Motown Records
personnel: Lionel Richie – vocals, saxophones, keyboards Milan Williams – keyboards Thomas McClary – vocals, guitars

tracks.t: Girl, I Think The World About You
Just To Be Close To You

about: The Commodores' fourth Motown album, produced with James Anthony Carmichael. It was their first to top the US R&B album chart and features the Lionel Richie ballad Just to Be Close to You, which also became a pop top ten hit.

title: Left My Blues In San Francisco
label: Chess Records
personnel: Buddy Guy - lead guitar & lead vocals Gene Barge - tenor saxophone
Reggie Boyd - bass guitar Matt "Guitar" Murphy - guitar Phil Thomas - drums

tracks.t: She Suits Me To A Tee

about: Buddy Guy's first album, released by Chess and assembled from sessions dating from 1962 to 1967 with producer Gene Barge. It pairs older blues material with a few Guy originals, adding horns and arrangements partly by Charles Stepney.

title: A Josh White Program
label: Warner Bros Records

tracks.t: I'm Gonna Move To The Outskirts Of Town
He Never Said A Mumblin' Word
I Want You And I Need You

about: A 1954 collection by folk and blues singer and guitarist Josh White, presenting a program of his songs. Detailed release information is sparse, and it is generally catalogued as a compilation.

title: Exile On Main St.
label: Rolling Stones Records
personnel: Mick Jagger – vocals; harmonica; electric guitar
Keith Richards – guitars, backing vocals; bass guitar; electric piano
Mick Taylor – guitars; bass guitar Bill Wyman – bass guitar

tracks.t: I Just Want To See His Face

about: A double album by the Rolling Stones, much of it recorded in a villa in the south of France while the band lived abroad for tax reasons. It topped charts in the UK and US, includes Tumbling Dice, and is widely ranked among the greatest rock albums.

title: Rare Stamps
label: Stax Records

tracks.t: You Can't Get Away From It
Just The One (I've Been Looking For)
I've Got To Love Somebody's Baby
If I Had To Do It All Over

about: A Stax collection of earlier singles by soul and blues vocalist Johnnie Taylor, gathering material recorded for the label before his breakthrough with Who's Making Love.

title: Europe '72
label: Warner Bros. Records
personnel: Bob Weir – rhythm guitar, vocals Phil Lesh – bass guitar, vocals
Keith Godchaux – piano Ron "Pigpen" McKernan – organ, harmonica, vocals Bill Kreutzmann – drums
about: A triple live album drawn from the Grateful Dead's spring 1972 European tour, issued by Warner Bros. Several new songs debuted on it, including Jack Straw and Brown-Eyed Women, and it became one of the band's best-selling releases.

title: Cosmic Thing
label: Reprise Records
personnel: Fred Schneider – vocals Cindy Wilson – vocals Kate Pierson – vocals, keyboards Keith Strickland – guitars, keyboards, backing vocals
about: The B-52's fifth album and the first after guitarist Ricky Wilson's death, produced by Nile Rodgers and Don Was for Reprise. Fueled by Love Shack and Roam, it became the group's biggest commercial success.

title: Black Moses
label: Enterprise
personnel: Isaac Hayes - vocals, piano, vibraphone, organ, electric piano The Isaac Hayes Movement: Ronnie Hudson - bass
Lester Snell - electric piano. Chalres "Skip" Pitts - guitar

tracks.t: (They Long To Be) Close To You
Nothing Takes The Place Of You
Medley: Ike's Rap II / Help Me Love
Medley: Ike's Rap III / Your Love Is So Doggone Good
I'll Never Fall In Love Again
Medley: Ike's Rap IV / A Brand New Me

about: A double album by Isaac Hayes on Stax's Enterprise imprint, issued soon after his Shaft soundtrack. It consists mostly of lengthy, orchestral reworkings of songs by other writers, and its fold-out cover depicting Hayes in robes became well known.

title: L.A. Woman
label: Elektra Records
personnel: Jim Morrison – vocals Ray Manzarek – keyboards, rhythm guitar, Rhodes piano
Robby Krieger – lead guitar John Densmore – drums Jerry Scheff – bass

tracks.t: The WASP (Texas Radio And The Big Beat)

about: The sixth studio album by the Doors, issued by Elektra and co-produced by the band with Bruce Botnick. It returned the group to a blues-rock sound, yielded the singles Love Her Madly and Riders on the Storm, and was the final record released while Jim Morrison was alive.

title: Led Zeppelin
label: Atlantic Records
personnel: Robert Plant – lead vocal, harmonica Jimmy Page – electric, acoustic and pedal steel guitars, backing vocal John Paul Jones – bass, organ, backing vocal John Bonham – drums, timpani, backing vocal
about: The first album by the English rock band Led Zeppelin, released in the US in January 1969 and in the UK that March. Often called Led Zeppelin I, it set out the heavy blues-based rock style that the group would become famous for.

title: Portrait
label: Bell Records
personnel: Billy Davis, Jr. - vocals Florence LaRue - vocals Marilyn McCoo - vocals Lamonte McLemore - vocals Ron Townson - vocals
about: The fifth album by the vocal group the 5th Dimension and their first for Bell Records, produced by Bones Howe in Hollywood. Boosted by the hit One Less Bell to Answer, it climbed to number 20 on the Billboard albums chart.

title: The Big Chill (Original Motion Picture Soundtrack)
label: Motown

tracks.t: Marvin Gaye: I Heard It Through The Grapevine
Smokey Robinson & The Miracles: The Tracks Of My Tears
Three Dog Night: Joy To The World
The Temptations: Ain't Too Proud To Beg
Aretha Franklin: (You Make Me Feel Like A) Natural Woman
Smokey Robinson & The Miracles: I Second That Emotion
Procol Harum: A Whiter Shade Of Pale

about: A various-artists soundtrack to the 1983 Lawrence Kasdan film The Big Chill, released by Motown. It gathers 1960s soul and rock hits heard in the movie, from acts such as Marvin Gaye, the Temptations and Aretha Franklin, and became a long-running commercial success.

title: Empty Bed Blues
label: Elektra Records

tracks.t: His Eye Is On The Sparrow

about: An LP by folk and blues singer and guitarist Josh White, issued by Elektra in early 1962 with Jac Holzman as producer. It was released in mono and stereo editions in the US and also appeared on labels in France and the UK.

title: The Beat
label: Columbia Records
personnel: Paul Collins – rhythm guitar, lead vocals Steven Huff – bass, second vocals Larry Whitman – lead guitar, third vocals Michael Ruiz – drums, percussion
about: The first album by the Los Angeles power pop band the Beat, fronted by Paul Collins, who wrote nearly all of its twelve songs. Bruce Botnick produced it in Hollywood studios for Columbia, and critics generally received it well.

title: Thriller
label: Epic
about: Michael Jackson's sixth studio album, released by Epic and produced with Quincy Jones. It spawned a string of hit singles including Billie Jean, Beat It and the title track, and it is widely cited as the best-selling album in history.

title: The Hunter
label: Chrysalis Records
personnel: Deborah Harry – vocals Chris Stein – guitar Frank Infante – guitar
Jimmy Destri – keyboards Nigel Harrison – bass

tracks.t: (Can I) Find The Right Words (To Say)
The Hunter Gets Captured By The Game

about: Blondie's sixth studio album, produced by Mike Chapman and recorded at the Hit Factory in New York for Chrysalis. It reached the UK top ten but was seen as a commercial and critical letdown, and the band issued no further new music until 1999.

title: Open Up The Door
label: Liberty
personnel: Billy Connolly Tam Harvey Gerry Rafferty

tracks.t: All The Best People Do It

about: The third and last studio album by the Glasgow folk duo the Humblebums, featuring Billy Connolly and Gerry Rafferty. It came out on Transatlantic Records in 1970, shortly before the pair split to pursue separate careers.

title: Welcome To The Pleasuredome
label: Island Records
personnel: Holly Johnson – lead vocals Paul Rutherford – backing vocals Brian Nash – guitar

tracks.t: Two Tribes (For The Victims Of Ravishment)

about: The first album by Liverpool band Frankie Goes to Hollywood, originally a double LP on ZTT produced by Trevor Horn. It collected hits such as Relax and Two Tribes, went to number one in the UK and earned triple platinum certification there.

title: Endless Honeymoon
label: Alimony Records
personnel: Sheila GRoves – vocals Linda Wilson – keyboards Robin Pfefer – guitar, vocals Libby Shriek – guitar, vocals Brian Marshall – bass, vocals Wendy Behrbaum – drums

title: Baby Grand
label: Arista Records
personnel: Eric Bazilian Rob Hyman David Kagan Rick Chertoff
about: The self-titled first LP by Philadelphia band Baby Grand, issued by Arista and produced by Rick Chertoff and Rob Hyman. The group included Hyman and Eric Bazilian, who later formed the Hooters; Billboard flagged the record as a top album pick in late 1977.

title: City Of Angels
label: Tamla
personnel: Billy Griffin – lead vocals, guitar, co-composer Bobby Rogers – backing vocals Pete Moore – backing vocals, producer, co-composer Ronnie White – backing vocals
about: A concept album by the Miracles on Motown's Tamla label, written by Billy Griffin and Pete Moore and produced by Freddie Perren and Moore. It follows a man chasing a former girlfriend to Los Angeles, and its single Love Machine became a number one pop hit.

title: License To Dream
label: Atlantic Records
personnel: Woodrow "Woody" Cunningham - lead vocals, drums Paul Crutchfield - keyboards, percussion Richard Lee - guitar Norman Durham - bass

tracks.t: Where Would I Be (Without Your Love)

about: The third album by New York funk band Kleeer, released by Atlantic Records. It reached number 13 on the Billboard soul albums chart, helped by the single Get Tough, which was a top five dance hit.

title: East Bay Grease
label: San Francisco Records
personnel: Rufus Miller - lead vocals Emilio Castillo - alto saxophone, vocals David Garibaldi - drums, vibes, vocals
Greg Adams - 1st trumpet. Stephen "Doc" Kupka - baritone saxophone, background vocals Skip Mesquite - tenor saxophone, flute, vocals
David Padron - 2nd trumpet Rocco Prestia - bass
Rick Stevens - background vocals Willy Fulton - guitar, background vocals Mic Gillette - trumpet, trombone, flugelhorn

tracks.t: The Skunk, The Goose, And The Fly

about: The first album by the Oakland soul and funk group Tower of Power, produced by David Rubinson and recorded in San Francisco. It introduced the band's horn-driven sound before they moved to Warner Bros. for Bump City.

title: The Age Of Aquarius
label: Soul City
personnel: Billy Davis, Jr. - vocals Florence LaRue - vocals Marilyn McCoo - vocals Lamonte McLemore - vocals Ron Townson - vocals

tracks.t: Medley: Aquarius/Let The Sunshine In (The Flesh Failures)
Don'tcha Hear Me Callin' To Ya

about: The fourth studio album by the 5th Dimension, produced by Bones Howe for Soul City. Its medley Aquarius/Let the Sunshine In won the Grammy for Record of the Year, and the album peaked at number two in the US and went gold.

title: Let's Take It To The Stage
label: Westbound Records
personnel: Vocals: 'Cool' Cal Simon, 'Bad Bosco' Bernie Worrell, C 'Boogie' Mosson, Garry 'Dowop' Shider, 'Sting' Ray Davis, 'Shady' Grady Thomas, Clarence "Fuzzy" Haskins Maggot Overlord: George Clinton Congas: Calvin Simon. Keyboards: Bernie Worrell. Bass: C Boogie Mosson Guitar: Eddie Hazel, Michael Hampton, Garry Shider

tracks.t: Let's Take It To The Stage
Get Off Your Ass And Jam
Baby I Owe You Something Good

about: The seventh studio album by Funkadelic, produced by George Clinton and released on Westbound. A funk rock record full of humor and jabs at rival acts, it reached number 14 on the Billboard R&B albums chart.

title: Stardust
label: Columbia Records

tracks.t: On The Sunny Side Of The Street

about: A collection of ten pop standards recorded by Willie Nelson with producer Booker T. Jones for Columbia. Despite label doubts, it topped the country albums chart, stayed on the charts for years and was eventually certified five times platinum.

title: Shaft
label: Enterprise Records
personnel: Isaac Hayes - Lead vocals, keyboards, and lyrics. The Bar-Kays and The Isaac Hayes Movement: Lester Snell - Electric piano
Gary Jones - conga, bongo drums. Richard "Johnny" Davis - trumpet
about: Isaac Hayes's double-LP score for the 1971 MGM film Shaft, issued on Stax's Enterprise label. Mostly instrumental, it topped the Billboard 200, and its title theme reached number one and won an Academy Award; it was later added to the National Recording Registry.

title: Easter
label: Arista Records
personnel: Patti Smith – vocals, guitar Lenny Kaye – guitar, bass guitar, vocals Jay Dee Daugherty – drums, percussion Ivan Král – bass guitar, vocals, guitar Bruce Brody – keyboards, synthesizer
about: The third studio album by Patti Smith and the second credited to the Patti Smith Group, produced by Jimmy Iovine for Arista. It was her commercial breakthrough, driven by the single Because the Night, co-written with Bruce Springsteen.

title: Shades Of Blue
label: Sunset Records

Billie Holiday:  Blue Turning Grey Over YouB2
Al Hibbler:  I Surrender Dear Al Hibbler:  I Got It Bad And That Ain't Good
Al Hibbler:  Don't Take Your Love From Me

about: A 1968 budget LP on the Sunset label that splits its sides between earlier recordings by jazz singer Billie Holiday and baritone Al Hibbler. Holiday sings songs such as Detour Ahead and Rocky Mountain Blues, while Hibbler covers standards like I Got It Bad and That Ain't Good.

title: Legend
label: ABC Records
personnel: Paul Cotton – lead guitar, vocals Rusty Young – steel guitar, guitars, vocals Charlie Harrison – bass, harmony vocals Steve Chapman – drums
about: Poco's eleventh studio album, a country rock record produced by Richard Sanford Orshoff for ABC. It reached number 14 on the Billboard 200 and went gold, supported by the hits Crazy Love and Heart of the Night.

title: Double Trouble
label: Charlie's Records
about: An album by Montserrat soca singer Arrow, released shortly before his international breakthrough with Hot Hot Hot. Wikipedia lists it among his early-1980s releases.

title: Freedom At Point Zero
label: Grunt Records
personnel: Mickey Thomas – lead and backing vocals
Paul Kantner – lead and backing vocals, rhythm guitar, keyboards
Pete Sears – bass, piano, electric piano, organ, rhythm guitar
about: The fifth studio album by Jefferson Starship and the first with singer Mickey Thomas after the departures of Grace Slick and Marty Balin. Produced by Ron Nevison for Grunt, it took the band toward harder rock and featured the hit Jane.

title: Chicago III
label: Columbia Records

tracks.t: A Hard Risin' Morning Without Breakfast
When All The Laughter Dies In Sorrow

about: The third studio album by the rock band Chicago, another double LP produced by James William Guercio for Columbia. It climbed to number two on the Billboard 200 and was later certified platinum in the US.

title: Year Of The Cat
label: Janus Records
personnel: Al Stewart - vocals, guitar, keyboards Peter White, Tim Renwick - guitar Peter Wood, Don Lobster - keyboards George Ford - bass

tracks.t: If It Doesn't Come Naturally, Leave It

about: Al Stewart's seventh studio album, produced by Alan Parsons and recorded partly at Abbey Road. Its title song became a US top ten hit, and the album reached number five on the Billboard 200 and went platinum.

title: Shinin' On
label: Capitol Records
personnel: Mark Farner – guitar, guitarrón, harmonica, organ, vocals Craig Frost – organ, clavinet, moog, piano, mellotron, backing vocals Mel Schacher – bass Don Brewer – drums, percussion, vocals
about: The eighth studio album by Grand Funk Railroad, produced by Todd Rundgren and released by Capitol. Its cover of The Loco-Motion went to number one, and early copies came with 3D glasses for artwork designed by Neal Adams.

title: The Captain And Me
label: Warner Bros. Records
personnel: Tom Johnston – guitar, ARP synthesizer, lead and backing vocals Patrick Simmons – guitar, ARP synthesizer, lead and backing vocals Tiran Porter – bass, backing vocals
John Hartman – drums, percussion Michael Hossack – drums, congas, timbales
about: The third studio album by the Doobie Brothers, produced by Ted Templeman for Warner Bros. It contains the hits Long Train Runnin' and China Grove, peaked at number seven in the US and has been certified double platinum.

title: Say It Loud I'm Black And I'm Proud
label: King Records
personnel: James Brown – Lead vocal Clyde Stubblefield – drums. 'Sweet Charles' Sherell – bass Jimmy Nolen – guitar
Maceo Parker – sax Fred Wesley - trombone

Say It Loud  - I'm Black And I'm Proud (Pt. 2)
I Guess I'll Have To Cry, Cry, Cry
Then You Can Tell Me Goodbye

about: An album by James Brown on King Records built around his 1968 single of the same name, which became an anthem of Black pride. It mixes funk tracks with other material recorded by Brown and his band in the late 1960s.

title: Hey Now Hey (The Other Side Of The Sky)
label: Atlantic Records
personnel: Aretha Franklin – lead vocals, acoustic piano Spooner Oldham – keyboards
Wayne Jackson – trumpet. Willie Bridges, Charles Chalmers, Andrew Love, Floyd Newman – saxophone

tracks.t: Hey Now Hey (The Other Side Of The Sky)
That's The Way I Feel About Cha

about: An Atlantic album by Aretha Franklin produced together with Quincy Jones, leaning toward jazz-influenced arrangements. It included the single Angel, written by her sister Carolyn Franklin, which became an R&B hit.

title: Visions
label: Columbia Records
personnel: Gladys Knight Merald "Bubba" Knight William Guest Edward Patten
about: Columbia Records release that marked a comeback for Gladys Knight & the Pips, with the group producing roughly half the tracks themselves. It reached No. 34 on the Billboard album chart, and its single Save the Overtime (For Me) topped the Black Singles chart.

title: After The Snow
label: Sire
personnel: Robbie Grey – vocals Gary McDowell – guitars Stephen Walker – keyboards Michael Conroy – bass, violin Richard Brown – drums, percussion
about: Second album by the Colchester new wave band Modern English, co-produced with Hugh Jones and issued by 4AD in Britain and Sire in America. It contains the international hit I Melt with You and was eventually certified gold in the United States.

title: Give The People What They Want
label: Arista Records
personnel: Ray Davies – guitar, keyboards, vocals Dave Davies – guitar, vocals Jim Rodford – bass Mick Avory – drums Ian Gibbons – keyboards

tracks.t: Give The People What They Want

about: Arista-era Kinks record produced by Ray Davies, continuing the band's arena-rock phase of the early 1980s. Singles taken from it included Better Things, Destroyer and Predictable.

title: Gold-Diggers Sound
label: Columbia Records
about: Third album from Texas soul singer Leon Bridges, issued by Columbia and named after the Los Angeles studio complex where it was made, with producers including Ricky Reed and Nate Mercereau. It entered the Billboard 200 at No. 17 and earned a Grammy nomination for Best R&B Album.

title: The Bonny
label: Little Runaway Records
about: Second album by Glasgow singer-songwriter Gerry Cinnamon, released independently on his own Little Runaway label. It debuted at No. 1 in the UK, Scotland and Ireland and was later certified platinum by the BPI.

title: Natty Dread
label: Tuff Gong
personnel: Bob Marley – lead vocals, rhythm guitar Aston Barrett – bass guitar Carlton Barrett – drums, percussion Bernard "Touter" Harvey – piano, organ Jean Roussel – Hammond organ, keyboards
about: Island Records album that was Bob Marley's first without founding Wailers Peter Tosh and Bunny Wailer. It features the original studio version of No Woman, No Cry along with Lively Up Yourself and Them Belly Full, and it later went gold in the UK.

title: Catch A Fire
label: Tuff Gong
personnel: Bob Marley – guitar, vocals Peter Tosh – organ, guitar, piano, vocals Bunny Wailer – bongos, conga, vocals Aston "Family Man" Barrett – bass guitar. Carlton "Carlie" Barrett – drums Rita Marley – backing vocals

tracks.t: Baby We've Got A Date (Rock It Baby)

about: The Wailers' first album for Island Records, recorded in Jamaica and then remixed in London by Chris Blackwell with added rock overdubs, including guitar by session player Wayne Perkins. It helped introduce reggae to an international rock audience.

title: The Colour And The Shape
label: RCA Records
personnel: Dave Grohl – lead vocals, guitar, drums Pat Smear – guitar Nate Mendel – bass
about: Second Foo Fighters album and the first made as a full band, produced by Gil Norton, with Dave Grohl re-recording most drum parts after William Goldsmith left. Its singles Monkey Wrench, Everlong and My Hero became rock radio staples, and it reached No. 10 in the US.

title: The Velvet Underground & Nico
label: Verve Records
personnel: Lou Reed – vocals, lead guitar, ostrich guitar
John Cale – electric viola, piano, bass, vocals, celesta, hissing
about: Debut album by the Velvet Underground featuring German singer Nico, nominally produced by Andy Warhol, who also designed its famous banana cover. It sold poorly and peaked at No. 129 on release but later became one of the most influential rock records, entering the National Recording Registry.

title: The Troublemaker
label: Columbia Records
personnel: Dan Spears - double bass Jeff Gutcheon - organ
Jimmy Day - pedal steel guitar Bobbie Nelson - piano

tracks.t: When The Roll Is Called Up Yonder

about: Country gospel collection by Willie Nelson, cut over two days in New York in 1973 with producer Arif Mardin but held back until Columbia issued it in 1976. It topped the Billboard country albums chart, and Uncloudy Day became a top-five country single.

title: City Of New Orleans
label: Columbia Records
personnel: Willie Nelson - vocals, guitar Reggie Young, J.R
Cobb, Chips Moman - guitar Mike Leech - bass
Bobby Emmons, Bobby Wood - keyboards Gene Chrisman - drums
Mickey Raphael - harmonica Wayne Jackson - trumpet

Why Are You Pickin' On Me
Until It's Time For You To Go

about: Mostly covers album by Willie Nelson, produced by Chips Moman for Columbia. His take on Steve Goodman's title song reached No. 1 on the country singles chart, and the record itself topped the country albums chart and went platinum in the US.

title: Mother's Milk
label: EMI
personnel: Anthony Kiedis – vocals John Frusciante – guitar, vocals Flea – bass, trumpet, vocals Chad Smith – drums, percussion, tambourine

tracks.t: Johnny Kick A Hole In The Sky

about: Red Hot Chili Peppers album produced by Michael Beinhorn and the first to feature guitarist John Frusciante and drummer Chad Smith. Its singles included a cover of Stevie Wonder's Higher Ground and Knock Me Down, and it became the band's first gold record.

title: Eddie Money
label: Columbia Records
personnel: Eddie Money – vocals, keyboards, harmonica, saxophone Jimmy Lyon – guitars
Gary Mallaber – drums, percussion Lonnie Turner – bass guitar
Gene Pardue – drums Bob "Pops" Popwell – bass guitar
Tom Scott – alto saxophone, tenor sax

tracks.t: You Really Got A Hold On Me
Wanna Be A Rock 'N' Roll Star
Save A Little Room In Your Heart For Me
So Good To Be In Love Again

about: Self-titled first album by rock singer Eddie Money, produced by Bruce Botnick for Columbia's Wolfgang imprint. Baby Hold On and Two Tickets to Paradise became radio hits, and the record went double platinum in the US.

title: The Completion Backward Principle

Roger Steen - Guitar, Vocals Prairie Prince - Drums
Vince Welnick - Keyboards, Vocals Rick Anderson - Bass

tracks.t: Attack Of The Fifty Foot Woman

about: The Tubes' first record for Capitol, produced by David Foster and presented with a mock corporate sales-seminar theme. Don't Want to Wait Anymore reached the Billboard top 40, and the album peaked at No. 36 in the US.

title: Big Science

about: First album by performance artist Laurie Anderson, co-produced with Roma Baran and drawing on her long stage work United States. It includes O Superman, which climbed to No. 2 on the UK singles chart after John Peel championed it.

title: Which One's Willie
label: Epic Records
personnel: Jimmy Hall Mike Duke. Jack Hall. T.K. Lively. Ricky Chancey Larry Berwald

tracks.t: Stop And Take A Look (At What You've Been Doing)/Don't Let The Green Grass Fool You
You Don't Know What You Mean To Me

about: Final studio album of Wet Willie's original run, issued by Epic Records. It contains the single Weekend, which reached No. 29 in the US, while the album itself peaked at No. 172 on the Billboard chart.

title: Below The Belt
label: Millennium Records
personnel: Billy Elworthy – lead and rhythm guitars

tracks.t: Any Way That You Want Me

about: Second album by New Jersey pop rock group Franke and the Knockouts, released on Millennium Records. It reached No. 48 on the US album chart and produced the top-25 single Without You (Not Another Lonely Night).

title: Star Wars
label: 20th Century Records

tracks.t: The Desert And The Robot Auction
Ben's Death And TIE Fighter Attack
The Land Of The Sand People
The Throne Room And End Title

about: Score for the 1977 film Star Wars, composed and conducted by John Williams and performed by the London Symphony Orchestra. The double LP reached No. 2 on the Billboard 200, went platinum, and the music won an Academy Award and several Grammys.

title: Darkness On The Delta
label: Fat Cat's Jazz
personnel: Wallace Davenport Walter "Slide" Harris Herb Hall John Eaton. Van Perry. Freddie Moore

tracks.t: When The Saints Go Marchin' In

about: Traditional New Orleans jazz set led by trumpeter Wallace Davenport, issued on Johnson McRee's Fat Cat's Jazz label and recorded around his visit to the Manassas jazz festival. Herb Hall plays clarinet, and the program includes standards such as Just a Closer Walk With Thee.

title: The Beginning Vol. 2
label: Mercury Records
about: Mercury LP by blues and folk singer Josh White, catalogued as MG 20821, revisiting material from the early part of his career. Songs include Paul and Silas, Lula, How Long and Goin' Down Slow.

title: Forbidden Island

about: Exotica album by Martin Denny for Liberty Records, recorded in Hollywood in early 1958 and the first made after vibraphonist Arthur Lyman left the group. It features several Denny originals, among them the title track and Primitiva.

Gil Baumgart – arranger, percussion Sandy Warner – cover model

tracks.t: The Queen Chant (E Lili Ua E)

about: Follow-up to Martin Denny's breakthrough Exotica, released on Liberty and produced by Si Waronker. It was recorded in 1957 with a lineup including Arthur Lyman on vibes and Augie Colon supplying bird calls and Latin percussion.

title: Touchdown
label: Tappan Zee Records
personnel: Bob James – electric piano, synthesizer, piano, producer, conductor, composed by
Howard Johnson – contrabass clarinet, baritone saxophone
Phil Bodner – alto saxophone, flute, oboe
Harvey Estrin – flute, clarinet, tenor saxophone
George Marge – tenor saxophone, english horn, flute, oboe, recorder

tracks.t: I Want To Thank You (Very Much)

about: Jazz fusion album by keyboardist Bob James on his Tappan Zee label. Its track Angela was adopted as the theme of the TV sitcom Taxi, and the record topped Billboard's jazz albums chart.

title: As The Screw Turns
label: Flamingo Time Records
personnel: Adam Scone - hammond organ Alex Chakour - guitar Caito Sanchez - drums, percussion Ian Hendrickson-Smith - sax Dave Guy - trumpet

tracks.t: My House Is Small (But I Dream Big)
They Say Its Christmas Time (Christmas Time In Brooklyn)

title: Are You Experienced?
label: Reprise Records
personnel: Jimi Hendrix – guitars, vocals, piano Noel Redding – bass guitar, backing vocals, rhythm guitar Mitch Mitchell – drums, percussion, backing vocals
about: First album by the Jimi Hendrix Experience, recorded in London with producer Chas Chandler. It reached No. 2 in Britain and No. 5 in the US, where the Reprise edition added hits like Purple Haze and Hey Joe, and it has gone multi-platinum.

title: Explores Your Mind
label: Motown Records
personnel: Al Green – vocals Teenie Hodges – guitar
Leroy Hodges – bass Charles Hodges – Hammond organ, piano
Howard Grimes – drums, congas Archie Turner, Michael Allen – piano Charles Chalmers, Donna Rhodes, Sandra Rhodes – backing vocals Andrew Love, Ed Logan – tenor sax
about: Hi Records album produced by Willie Mitchell and Al Green. It gave Green another No. 1 soul album and the top-ten pop hit Sha-La-La (Make Me Happy), and it introduced Take Me to the River, later covered by Talking Heads.

title: Dos
label: Warner Bros. Records
personnel: Arcelio García, Jr.: Vocals, percussion Jorge Santana: Guitar Abel Zarate: Guitars, vocals. Pablo Tellez: bass, percussion Richard Kermode: Keyboards, electric piano, organ, piano, percussion Francisco Aquabella: Conga, bongos, percussion, vocals Hadley Caliman: Tenor & baritone sax, flute
about: Second Warner Bros. album by San Francisco Latin rock band Malo, produced by David Rubinson, featuring guitarist Jorge Santana and singer Arcelio Garcia. It reached No. 62 on the Billboard 200.

title: Roots
label: Curtom Records
personnel: Curtis Mayfield - vocals, guitar Craig McMullen - guitar Joseph "Lucky" Scott - bass Tyrone McCullen - drums
Henry Gibson - percussion Leroy Hutson, Michael Hawkins - background vocals Johnny Pate, Riley Hampton - arrangements

tracks.t: Love To Keep You In My Mind

about: Second solo album by Curtis Mayfield, self-produced and released on his Curtom label. It reached No. 6 on the R&B albums chart and No. 40 on the pop chart, with songs such as Get Down and We Got to Have Peace.

title: The Toys Sing "A Lover's Concerto" And "Attack!"
label: Dynovoice Records
personnel: Barbara Harris - lead vocals Barbara Parritt June Montiero

tracks.t: Can't Get Enough Of You Baby

about: The only album by New York girl group The Toys, released on DynoVoice and produced by Sandy Linzer and Denny Randell. It collects their hits A Lover's Concerto and Attack! and reached the top ten of the R&B albums chart.

title: First Take
label: Atlantic Records
personnel: Roberta Flack – piano, vocals Bucky Pizzarelli – guitars
Ray Lucas – drums, percussion Seldon Powell, Frank Wess – sax
Charles McCracken, George Ricci – cello Benny Powell – trombone
Jimmy Nottingham, Joe Newman – trumpet Emanuel Green, Gene Orloff – violin
Alfred Brown, Selwart Clarke, Theodore Israel – viola

tracks.t: Hey, That's No Way To Say Goodbye
The First Time Ever I Saw Your Face
Ballad Of The Sad Young Men

about: Debut Atlantic album by Roberta Flack, produced by Joel Dorn. After Clint Eastwood used The First Time Ever I Saw Your Face in Play Misty for Me, the song became a No. 1 hit and the album topped the Billboard 200 in 1972.

title: Once Upon A Time
label: A&M Records
personnel: Jim Kerr – vocals Charlie Burchill – guitars Michael MacNeil – piano, synthesizers Mel Gaynor – drums, backing vocals John Giblin – bass
about: Simple Minds' seventh studio record was produced by Jimmy Iovine and Bob Clearmountain and issued by Virgin. It reached number one in Britain and the US top ten, helped by the hits Alive and Kicking, Sanctify Yourself and All the Things She Said.

title: High Violet
label: 4AD
personnel: Matt Berninger – lead vocals Aaron Dessner – guitars, keyboard, bass Bryce Dessner – guitars Bryan Devendorf – drums, percussion Scott Devendorf – bass, guitar
about: The fifth album by the Brooklyn indie rock group came out on 4AD after sessions in Brooklyn and Connecticut, largely self-produced with Peter Katis. It entered the Billboard 200 at number three, earned wide critical praise and won a Q Award for Best Album.

title: Extensions
label: Argo
personnel: Ahmad Jamal – piano Jamil Nasser – bass Vernel Fournier – drums
about: A jazz LP by pianist Ahmad Jamal, cut in New York in May 1965 and issued on the Argo label. Its four tracks open with a long Jamal original and also include pieces by John Handy and Benny Golson.

title: There's A Riot Goin' On
label: Sundazed Music
personnel: Sly Stone – drums, synthesizers, guitar, bass, keyboards, vocals Rose Stone – vocals, keyboards
Billy Preston – keyboards Jerry Martini – tenor sax
Freddie Stone – guitar Ike Turner – guitar
Larry Graham – bass, vocals Greg Errico – drums

tracks.t: Africa Talks To You "The Asphalt Jungle"
Thank You For Talkin' To Me Africa

about: Sly and the Family Stone's fifth album, released by Epic, is a darker and murkier funk record largely assembled by Sly Stone alone using heavy overdubs and a drum machine. It topped the US pop and soul album charts and its single Family Affair reached number one.

title: London Calling
label: Columbia Records
personnel: Joe Strummer – lead and backing vocals, rhythm guitar, piano Mick Jones – lead guitar, piano, harmonica, backing and lead vocals Paul Simonon – bass, backing vocals, lead vocals on "The Guns of Brixton" Topper Headon – drums, percussion
about: The Clash's third album was a double LP issued in Britain in December 1979, reaching North America the following month. Mixing punk with reggae, rockabilly and other styles, it has sold millions worldwide and regularly appears near the top of greatest-album rankings.

title: Then Play On
label: Reprise Records
personnel: Peter Green – vocals, guitar, harmonica, six string bass, percussion, cello
Danny Kirwan – vocals, guitar John McVie – bass Mick Fleetwood – drums, percussion
about: Fleetwood Mac's third album and first on Reprise broadened the group's blues base with folk, hard rock and psychedelic elements. It was the first record to feature Danny Kirwan and the final one with Peter Green, and it charted in the UK top ten.

tracks.t: Joshua Fought The Battle Of Jericho
Nobody Knows The Trouble I've Seen
Joshua Fit The Battle Of Jericho

title: The Rise And Fall Of Ziggy Stardust And The Spiders From Mars
label: Parlophone Records
personnel: David Bowie – vocals, acoustic guitar, saxophone, arrangements Mick Ronson – electric guitar, piano, backing vocals, organ, synthesiser Trevor Bolder – bass, trumpet
about: David Bowie's fifth album, co-produced with Ken Scott and recorded at Trident Studios, loosely follows an invented alien rock star named Ziggy Stardust. Backed by the Spiders from Mars, it became his commercial breakthrough and is among his best-selling and most celebrated records.

title: Feel My Soul
label: Perception Records
personnel: Bill Curtis - drums Johnny King - guitar
George Williams - trumpet Johnny Flippin - bass

tracks.t: Why Is It So Hard To Do

about: An early funk LP by the New York group the Fatback Band, credited with Brother Johnny King and issued on Perception Records in 1974. It came out before the band moved to Event Records and closes with a lengthy title track.

title: Amazing Grace
label: Atlantic Records
personnel: Aretha Franklin – piano, lead vocals Rev
Franklin - vocals. Kenneth "Ken" Lupper – organ, keyboards
Chuck Rainey – bass Southern California Community Choir – background vocals

tracks.t: Medley: Precious Lord, Take My Hand / You've Got A Friend
What A Friend We Have In Jesus
God Will Take Care Of You

about: A double gospel album captured over two nights in January 1972 at a Baptist church in Los Angeles, with Rev. James Cleveland and a community choir. It won a Grammy, went double platinum and stands as Aretha Franklin's top-selling release.

title: Venusian Summer
label: Nemperor Records
personnel: Lenny White - drums Doug Rauch - bass Onaje Allan Gumbs - piano Doug Rodrigues - guitar, vocals Raymon Gomez - guitar Jimmy Smith - organ

tracks.t: Away Go Troubles Down The Drain

about: The first solo record by Return to Forever drummer Lenny White, issued on Nemperor. This jazz fusion set features guest guitarists including Al Di Meola and Larry Coryell.

title: Seven And The Ragged Tiger
label: Capitol Records
personnel: Simon Le Bon – lead vocals Andy Taylor – guitars John Taylor – bass guitar Roger Taylor – drums Nick Rhodes – keyboards

tracks.t: (I'm Looking For) Cracks In The Pavement

about: Duran Duran's third album was recorded in France, Montserrat and Australia and leans more heavily on synthesizers than its predecessor. It gave the band its first UK number one album and spawned hits such as Union of the Snake and The Reflex.

title: Magical Mystery Tour
label: Capitol Records
personnel: John Lennon – vocals, guitar, piano, Mellotron, Hammond organ, electric piano, clavioline, harpsichord; bass harmonica, Jew's harp, banjo, percussion Paul McCartney – vocals, guitar, piano, Mellotron, harmonium; recorder, penny whistle, percussion George Harrison – vocals, guitar, Hammond organ, bass harmonica, swarmandal, violin, percussion Ringo Starr – drums and percussion
about: Songs tied to the Beatles' television film of the same name, issued in the US as an LP that added recent singles and in Britain as a double EP in December 1967. The material is rooted in psychedelic rock.

title: Movement
label: Factory
personnel: Bernard Sumner – vocals, guitars, melodica, synthesizers and programming Peter Hook – bass, vocals Gillian Gilbert – synthesizers and programming, guitars Stephen Morris – drums, synthesizers and programming
about: New Order's first album, produced by Martin Hannett for Factory Records, was made after Ian Curtis's death and carries over much of Joy Division's bleak post-punk mood with added synthesizers. It peaked at 30 in the UK and topped the independent chart.

title: It's Glitz
label: Grazer Records
personnel: Nick Allen - vocals, guitar Carlos Palacios - vocals, bass, piano Ray Searaphin - vocals, guitar Dan Rincon - drums

title: What's New Pussycat?
label: Parrot Records

tracks.t: Won't You Give Him (One More Chance)

about: Tom Jones's second album was put out by his American label Parrot to cash in on his theme song for the film What's New Pussycat?. Produced by Peter Sullivan, it gathers tracks dropped from his US debut, earlier B-sides and other recordings.

title: Live At Fillmore West Auditorium San Francisco, 9 April 1970
label: Radio Looploop
personnel: Miles Davis - trumpet Chick Corea - piano Dave Holland - bass Jack DeJohnette - drums Airto Moreira - percussion Steve Grossman - sax

tracks.t: I Fall In Love Too Easy

about: A double LP of a Miles Davis concert at the Fillmore West in San Francisco on 9 April 1970, issued in 2020 by the Radio Loop Loop label. The set list includes Directions, Spanish Key and Bitches Brew.

title: Taj Mahal
label: Columbia Records
personnel: Taj Mahal – vocals, guitar, harmonica, slide guitar, music arranger Jesse Ed Davis – lead guitar, slide guitar Ry Cooder – rhythm guitar, mandolin Bill Boatman – rhythm guitar
Gary Gilmore – bass. Sanford Konikoff, Chuck "Brother" Blackwell – drums
about: Taj Mahal's first album, released by Columbia, reworks older blues numbers in a blues-rock style with guitarists Jesse Ed Davis and Ry Cooder. It drew good reviews but did not chart.

title: Axis: Bold As Love
label: Legacy Records
personnel: Jimi Hendrix – vocals, electric guitar, piano, recorder Mitch Mitchell – drums, backing vocals Noel Redding – bass guitars (four- and eight-string), backing vocals
about: The Jimi Hendrix Experience's second album was recorded at Olympic Studios in London and produced by Chas Chandler. It reached the top five in both the UK and US and contains songs such as Little Wing and Spanish Castle Magic.

title: Their Satanic Majesties' Second Request
label: A Records
personnel: Anton Newcombe Brian Glaze, Dean Taylor Jeff Davies, Joel Gion Mara Kegal, Matt Hollywood
about: The fourth studio album by the San Francisco psychedelic band, one of three full-length records they issued in 1996. Its name and sound nod to the Rolling Stones' 1967 psychedelic album, and nearly all songs were written by Anton Newcombe.

title: Foo Fighters
label: Roswell Records
personnel: Dave Grohl – vocals, guitars, bass guitar, drums, production Greg Dulli – additional guitar on "X-Static" Barrett Jones – backing vocals
about: Dave Grohl recorded this debut in a week in late 1994, playing almost every instrument himself after Kurt Cobain's death. Released by Roswell and Capitol, it yielded singles like This Is a Call and Big Me and went platinum in the US.

title: French Kiss
label: Capitol Records
personnel: Bob Welch – vocals, guitar, bass guitar Alvin Taylor – drums

Mick Fleetwood – drums on "Sentimental Lady" Christine McVie – background vocals Lindsey Buckingham – guitar and background vocals on "Sentimental Lady" Gene Page – string arrangements Juice Newton – background vocals on "Ebony Eyes"
about: Bob Welch's first solo album on Capitol grew from songs intended for his band Paris and features former Fleetwood Mac colleagues as guests. It went platinum and produced the hits Sentimental Lady and Ebony Eyes.

title: Old Crest On A New Wave
label: Columbia
personnel: Dave Mason – vocals, guitars Mark Stein – pianos, organ, synthesizers, backing vocals Mike Finnigan – acoustic piano, organ
Jim Krueger – guitars Bob Glaub – bass
Ray Revis – percussion Michael Jackson – lead and backing vocals ("Save Me")

tracks.t: Tryin' To Get Back To You
Old Crest On A New Wave

about: A Columbia rock album by Dave Mason, co-produced with Joe Wissert in Hollywood. Its lone single, Save Me, featured Michael Jackson on backing vocals and made the lower half of the Billboard Hot 100.

title: Desolation Boulevard
label: Capitol Records
personnel: Brian Connolly – lead vocals Steve Priest – bass, lead vocals, backing vocals Andy Scott – guitars, synthesizer, lead vocals, backing vocals Mick Tucker – drums, percussion, backing vocals
about: The Sweet's third studio album first appeared on RCA in Europe in late 1974, with a differently sequenced Capitol edition following in North America in 1975. The US version added Ballroom Blitz and songs from the earlier Sweet Fanny Adams.

title: Vs.
label: Epic Records
personnel: Eddie Vedder – vocals; rhythm guitar Dave Abbruzzese – drums Jeff Ament – bass guitar; upright bass Stone Gossard – rhythm guitar Mike McCready – lead guitar

tracks.t: Elderly Woman Behind The Counter In A Small Town

about: Pearl Jam's second album, their first with producer Brendan O'Brien, set a first-week US sales record and held the top of the Billboard 200 for five weeks. Singles included Go, Daughter, Animal and Dissident.

title: Blue Train
label: Blue Note
personnel: John Coltrane – tenor saxophone Lee Morgan – trumpet Curtis Fuller – trombone Kenny Drew – piano Paul Chambers – bass Philly Joe Jones – drums
about: John Coltrane's only session as a leader for Blue Note, recorded at Rudy Van Gelder's studio in September 1957 with a sextet including Lee Morgan and Curtis Fuller. This hard bop record contains four Coltrane originals and one standard.

title: Super Taylor
label: Stax Records

tracks.t: At Night Time (My Pillow Tells A Tale)
It Don't Pay To Get Up In The Morning

about: A Stax LP by soul singer Johnnie Taylor, produced by Don Davis. It was recorded across studios in Muscle Shoals, Detroit and Memphis.

title: Rocky Road
label: United Artists Records
about: An instrumental LP issued by United Artists in 1976 under the name The New Ventures, a billing used by the Ventures. Its tracks include a version of Moonlight Serenade.

title: Perverted Monks
label: Reggae Lounge
personnel: Afu-Ra (Aaron Philip) Poisonous Taoist Solar Monk Aqua Monk Caged Monk
about: The third full-length release by Brooklyn rapper Afu-Ra, presented under the Perverted Monks banner alongside associated artists.

title: Room On Fire
label: RCA Records
personnel: Julian Casablancas – vocals Albert Hammond, Jr. – guitar Nick Valensi – guitar Nikolai Fraiture – bass guitar Fabrizio Moretti – drums
about: The Strokes followed their acclaimed debut with this RCA release, again produced by Gordon Raphael in New York. It reached the top five in the US and number two in Britain, and its singles included 12:51, Reptilia and The End Has No End.

title: Songs In The Key Of Life
label: Tamla
personnel: Stevie Wonder – lead vocals, musician, arrangement, composer, producer Nathan Watts – bass Raymond Pounds – drums
Greg Phillinganes – keyboards Michael Sembello – lead guitar

tracks.t: Love's In Need Of Love Today
Ngiculela - Es Una Historia - I Am Singing

about: Stevie Wonder's sprawling double LP with a bonus EP came out on Tamla and opened at number one in the US, staying there for thirteen weeks. I Wish and Sir Duke both topped the Hot 100, and the record won the Grammy for Album of the Year.

title: Shabooh Shoobah
label: ATCO Records
personnel: Michael Hutchence – vocals Tim Farriss – guitar Kirk Pengilly – guitar, saxophone, vocals Garry Gary Beers – bass guitar, vocals Jon Farriss – drums, percussion, vocals Andrew Farriss – keyboards, guitar
about: Produced by Mark Opitz, this INXS record gave the Australian band its first real breakthrough in the United States. It peaked at number five at home and featured singles such as The One Thing, Don't Change and To Look at You.

title: Katanga!
label: Pacific Jazz
personnel: Curtis Amy - tenor saxophone, soprano saxophone Dupree Bolton - trumpet Jack Wilson - piano Ray Crawford - guitar Victor Gaskin - bass Doug Sides - drums

tracks.t: You Don't Know What Love Is

about: Saxophonist Curtis Amy co-led this hard bop session with trumpeter Dupree Bolton, cutting it in Hollywood in February 1963 for Pacific Jazz under producer Richard Bock. Bolton wrote the title piece, and the long-unavailable album is now regarded as a rewarding rarity.

title: I Robot
label: Arista Records
personnel: Alan Parsons – keyboards, vocoder, backing vocals, acoustic guitar David Paton – bass, acoustic guitar, backing vocals Stuart Tosh – drums, percussion, backing vocals Ian Bairnson – electric and acoustic guitars, backing vocals Eric Woolfson – keyboards, vocoder, backing vocals Duncan Mackay – keyboards

tracks.t: I Wouldn't Want To Be Like You
Day After Day (The Show Must Go On)

about: Recorded at Abbey Road and issued by Arista, this concept record by the Alan Parsons Project draws loosely on Isaac Asimov's robot stories to explore artificial intelligence. It reached the US top ten and produced the single I Wouldn't Want to Be Like You.

title: Brother Where You Bound
label: A&M Records
personnel: Rick Davies – keyboards, lead vocals John Helliwell – saxophones Dougie Thomson – bass Bob Siebenberg – drums
about: This A&M release was Supertramp's first after Roger Hodgson left, with Rick Davies writing and singing everything. Its lengthy title track features David Gilmour on guitar and Orwell readings, while the single Cannonball became a US rock radio hit.

title: Reconciled
label: Elektra Records
personnel: Michael Been – lead vocals, bass, guitar, keyboards Tom Ferrier – guitar, vocals Scott Musick – drums, percussion, vocals Jim Goodwin – keyboards, vocals Joe Read – bass, vocals
about: The Call recorded this Elektra album at the Power Station in New York with guest contributions from Peter Gabriel, Jim Kerr and Robbie Robertson. It reached number 82 in the US, and its songs I Still Believe and Everywhere I Go found an audience on rock and college radio.

title: Snakes And Ladders
label: United Artists Records
personnel: Gerry Rafferty – vocals, acoustic guitar Mo Foster, Pete Zorn – bass Billy Livsey – piano Ian Lynn – keyboards Jerry Donahue, Richard Brunton – guitar
about: Gerry Rafferty co-produced this United Artists album with Hugh Murphy. It climbed to number 15 in Britain but only 61 in the US, and its singles Bring It All Home and The Royal Mile were modest chart entries.

title: It's Just Begun
label: Tidal Waves Music
personnel: Jimmy Castor - Saxophone, Timbales, Vocals Doug Gibson - Bass, Backing Vocals Harry Jensen - Guitar Lenny Fridie, Jr. - Congas Gerry Thomas - Trumpet, Piano

tracks.t: You Better Be Good (Or The Devil Gon' Getcha)

about: Issued by RCA, this funk album by the Jimmy Castor Bunch reached number 27 on the Billboard 200, helped by the top-ten single Troglodyte (Cave Man). Its title track later became a favourite of breakdancers and one of the most sampled pieces in hip-hop.

title: Coda
label: Swan Song
personnel: Robert Plant – lead vocals, harmonica John Bonham – drums, percussion John Paul Jones – bass guitar, piano, keyboards Jimmy Page – acoustic and electric guitars, electronic treatments
about: Released on Swan Song about two years after John Bonham's death ended Led Zeppelin, this collection gathers unused studio and live recordings spanning the band's career. It reached the top ten in both Britain and the US and is often treated as their final album.

title: Free Your Mind And Your Ass Will Follow
label: Westbound Records
personnel: George Clinton – lead vocals Fuzzy Haskins, Calvin Simon, Grady Thomas, Ray Davis – vocals Eddie Hazel, Tawl Ross – guitar, vocals Bernie Worrell – Hammond organ, Vox organ, piano Billy Nelson – bass, vocals

tracks.t: Free Your Mind And Your Ass Will Follow
I Wanna Know If It's Good To You

about: Funkadelic's second Westbound release was produced by George Clinton in Detroit and blends heavy psychedelic rock with funk. Clinton later said the group tried to make the whole record while on acid. It reached number 11 on the Black albums chart.

title: Every 1's A Winner
label: Infinity Records
personnel: Errol Brown – lead vocals Harvey Hinsley – guitars, backing vocals Larry Ferguson – keyboards, Moog synthesizer Patrick Olive – bass guitar, backing vocals Tony Connor – drums

tracks.t: Love Is The Answer One More Time
Sometimes It Hurts To Be A Friend
I'm Going To Make You Feel Like A Woman

about: Produced by Mickie Most for RAK, this Hot Chocolate album includes the UK chart-topper So You Win Again and the title song, which became a top-ten hit in the US. The LP itself charted around number 30 on both sides of the Atlantic.

title: Exodus
label: Tuff Gong Records
personnel: Bob Marley - lead and backing vocals, guitars Junior Marvin - electric guitars Aston Barrett - basses. Carlton Barrett: drums Tyrone Downie - synthesizer, electric piano, organ and backing vocals Alvin "Seeco" Patterson - percussions
about: Partly recorded in London after Bob Marley left Jamaica following an attempt on his life, this Island release spawned Jamming, Waiting in Vain and Three Little Birds. Time magazine later picked it as the finest album of the twentieth century.

title: Lionel Richie
label: Motown Records
personnel: Lionel Richie – vocals, acoustic piano, Fender Rhodes

tracks.t: Just Put Some Love In Your Heart

about: Lionel Richie's first solo record after leaving the Commodores was co-produced with James Anthony Carmichael for Motown. It reached number three in the US and topped the R&B chart, with Truly hitting number one and You Are and My Love also scoring big.

title: Movin' On
label: Motown Records
personnel: Lionel Richie – vocals, saxophones, keyboards Milan Williams – keyboards Thomas McClary – vocals, guitars Ronald LaPread – bass Walter Orange – vocals, drums, percussion
about: The Commodores made this Motown album with producer James Anthony Carmichael. It peaked at number 29 on the Billboard 200 and number seven on the R&B list, and the ballad Sweet Love became a top-five pop single.

title: Struggling Man
label: Island Records

tracks.t: Can't Stop Worrying, Can't Stop Loving You

about: Jimmy Cliff produced this Island Records LP himself, issued in Britain under catalogue ILPS 9235. The ten songs, including the title track and Better Days Are Coming, focus on perseverance and social hope.

title: Go West
label: Casablanca Records
personnel: Glenn Hughes - Leather man David Hodo - Construction worker
Randy Jones - Cowboy Russell Dabney - drums
Alfonso Carey - bass. Jimmy (Nails) Lee - guitar Rodger Lee - guitar
about: Produced by Jacques Morali for Casablanca, this disco album by Village People reached the US top ten. It contains In the Navy, a major hit in America and Britain, and the title song that the Pet Shop Boys later revived.

title: Back In Black
label: Atlantic Records
personnel: Brian Johnson – lead vocals Angus Young – lead guitar Malcolm Young – rhythm guitar, backing vocals Cliff Williams – bass guitar, backing vocals Phil Rudd – drums

tracks.t: What Do You Do For Money Honey
Let Me Put My Love Into You
You Shook Me All Night Long
Rock And Roll Ain't Noise Pollution

about: AC/DC's first album with Brian Johnson, who joined after Bon Scott's death, was produced by Mutt Lange. It went to number one in Britain and Australia and is reckoned among the biggest-selling records ever, with around 50 million copies sold.

title: The Final Cut
label: Columbia Records
personnel: Roger Waters – lead vocals (all tracks), bass, acoustic guitar, synthesizers David Gilmour – lead and rhythm guitars, vocals Nick Mason – drums

tracks.t: Get Your Filthy Hands Off My Desert

about: Conceived by Roger Waters from leftover Wall material and reshaped into an anti-war statement after the Falklands conflict, this was his last Pink Floyd record and the only one without Richard Wright. It topped the UK chart but drew mixed reviews and no tour.

title: Soulin'
label: Capitol Records

tracks.t: So Hard To Laugh, So Easy To Cry
It Was A Very Good Year
On A Clear Day (You Can See Forever)
Breaking My Back (Instead Of Using My Mind)

about: Produced by David Axelrod with arrangements by H. B. Barnum, this Capitol LP pairs soul numbers with standards and spoken monologues. It includes Love Is a Hurtin' Thing, which topped the R&B singles chart in late 1966, and the album earned gold status.

title: Say No To The Devil
label: Original Blues Classics
personnel: Blind Gary Davis – guitar, 12 string guitar, harmonica, vocals

tracks.t: Lord, I Looked Down The Road
No One Can Do Me Like Jesus
Tryin' To Get To Heaven In Due Time

about: Reverend Gary Davis recorded this gospel blues set at the Van Gelder Studio in 1961, and Bluesville issued it the following year with Kenneth Goldstein producing. It followed A Little More Faith in his run of Prestige-related albums.

title: A Love Supreme
label: Impulse!
personnel: John Coltrane – bandleader, liner notes, vocals, tenor saxophone, saxophone Jimmy Garrison – double bass Elvin Jones – drums, gong, timpani McCoy Tyner – piano
about: John Coltrane cut this four-part devotional suite with his classic quartet in a single December 1964 session at Van Gelder Studio for Impulse. Widely celebrated as a jazz landmark, it was later added to the US National Recording Registry.

title: Never Mind The Bollocks Here's The Sex Pistols
label: Warner Bros. Records
personnel: Johnny Rotten – lead vocals Steve Jones – guitar, bass guitar, backing vocals Paul Cook – drums Glen Matlock – bass guitar on "Anarchy in the UK" Sid Vicious – bass guitar on "Bodies" and "God Save the Queen"
about: The only studio album by the Sex Pistols was produced by Chris Thomas and Bill Price and issued by Virgin. Despite shop bans and an obscenity case over its title, it entered the UK chart at number one and is regarded as a cornerstone of punk.

title: Willy And The Poor Boys
label: Fantasy Records
personnel: John Fogerty – vocals, lead guitar, piano, maracas, cowbell, harmonica Tom Fogerty – rhythm guitar, backing vocals Stu Cook – bass, washtub bass, backing vocals Doug Clifford – drums, washboard

tracks.t: It Came Out Of The Sky
Don't Look Now (It Ain't You Or Me)

about: Creedence Clearwater Revival's third album of 1969 was produced by John Fogerty for Fantasy. Built loosely around a fictional jug band, it reached number three in the US and carried the double-sided hit Down on the Corner and Fortunate Son.

title: The Turning Point
label: Polydor Records
personnel: John Mayall – guitar, harmonica, keyboards, tambourine, vocals, slide guitar John Almond – flute, saxophone, alto saxophone, tenor saxophone Jon Mark – acoustic guitar Steve Thompson – bass guitar

tracks.t: I'm Gonna Fight For You J.B.

about: John Mayall taped this drummerless acoustic-leaning blues concert at the Fillmore East in July 1969 with Jon Mark, Steve Thompson and Johnny Almond. Polydor released it later that year, and it marked a sharp change from his earlier electric bands.

title: Spirituals & Blues
label: Elektra Records

tracks.t: Nobody Knows The Trouble I've Seen
Just A Closer Walk With Thee
I Don't Intend To Die In Egypt Land

about: Josh White recorded this ten-track mono LP for Elektra, produced by Jac Holzman and Mark Abramson. It mixes gospel spirituals with blues material such as Silicosis Blues and Nobody Knows the Trouble I've Seen.

title: Mothership Connection
label: Casablanca Records
personnel: George Clinton - vocals Calvin Simon, Fuzzy Haskins, Ray Davis, Grady Thomas, Gary Shider, Glenn Goins, Bootsy Collins - vocals. Fred Wesley, Maceo Parker, Michael Brecker, Randy Brecker, Boom, Joe Farrell - horns
Bootsy Collins, Cordell Mosson - bass. Garry Shider, Michael Hampton, Glenn Goins, Bootsy Collins - guitar. Tiki Fulwood, Jerome Brailey, Bootsy Collins, Gary Cooper - drums

tracks.t: P. Funk (Wants To Get Funked Up)
Give Up The Funk (Tear The Roof Off The Sucker)

about: George Clinton produced this space-themed concept album for Casablanca, launching much of the P-Funk mythology. It went platinum, featured Tear the Roof Off the Sucker, and was later chosen for the Library of Congress National Recording Registry.

title: Black Power
label: Now-Again Records
personnel: Bruce Kaunda Joe Kunda Saul Manda Teddy Makombe
about: Zambian Zamrock group The Peace recorded this album around 1973 to 1974 and released it on the ZMPL label. Its love-and-peace lyrics and psychedelic funk sound make it unusual in the scene, and it is the band's only surviving release.

title: I Learned The Hard Way
label: Daptone Records
personnel: Neal Sugarman – tenor sax. Fernando "Boogaloo" Velez – bongos, congas, tambourine

tracks.t: She Ain't A Child No More

about: Produced by Gabriel Roth for Daptone, this retro soul record by Sharon Jones and the Dap-Kings became the group's highest-charting album to that point, reaching number 15 on the Billboard 200 and number six on the R&B chart.

title: The Freewheelin' Bob Dylan
label: Columbia Records
personnel: Bob Dylan – acoustic guitar, harmonica, vocals

tracks.t: Don't Think Twice, It's All Right
Honey, Just Allow Me One More Chance

about: Bob Dylan's second LP on Columbia, made up mostly of his own songs rather than folk covers. It includes Blowin' in the Wind, A Hard Rain's a-Gonna Fall and Don't Think Twice, It's All Right, and it established him as a major songwriter.

title: How 'Bout Us
label: Columbia Records
personnel: Pauli Carman Rena Day Dana Walden Michael Reed Rocky Maffit Howard Reeder
about: First studio album by the Illinois R&B group Champaign, issued in 1981 on Columbia. Its title song became the band's signature hit, reaching the US top 20 and the UK top five.

label: Other People

tracks.t: This Old House Is All I Have
You're Going To Love Me And Scream

about: First full-length record Nicolás Jaar issued under his Against All Logic alias, released with little warning on his Other People label. It gathers house and sample-based dance tracks made over the preceding years, and some critics treat it as a compilation.

title: Super Fly (Original Motion Picture Soundtrack)
label: Rhino Vinyl
personnel: Curtis Mayfield – vocals, guitar, producer Phil Upchurch - guitar
Master Henry Gibson – percussion Morris Jennings – drums Craig McMullen – guitar
about: Curtis Mayfield's music for the blaxploitation film Super Fly, released on Curtom. The record topped the Billboard album chart and produced the hits Freddie's Dead and Superfly, with lyrics that commented critically on drug culture.

title: The Best Of Josh White
label: Elektra Records
personnel: Josh White – guitar, vocals Al Hall, Bill Lee – bass

tracks.t: Jesus Gonna Make Up My Dyin' Bed
The Story Of John Henry ... A Musical Narrative
