about: Archival release of a 1969 James Brown concert recorded in his hometown of Augusta, Georgia, originally intended for an album that was shelved. It was issued for the first time in 2019.

title: In Rainbows
label: XL Recordings
personnel: Colin Greenwood Jonny Greenwood Ed O'Brien Philip Selway Thom Yorke
about: Radiohead's seventh studio record, first sold as a download for which buyers chose their own price after the band left EMI. A physical release followed, and the album topped the UK and US charts and won Grammy awards.

title: Best Of Silver Convention
label: Midsong International
about: Hits collection by the Munich disco act Silver Convention, issued in 1978 only in Australia on the Hammard label. It gathers the group's best-known singles from the mid-1970s.

title: Dancing On The Ceiling
label: Motown
personnel: Lionel Richie – vocals, keyboards Michael Boddicker – synthesizers Carlos Rios, Tim May – guitar Greg Phillinganes – keyboards, synthesizers, drum machine Paul Leiim – drums
about: Lionel Richie's third solo studio record, following the huge success of Can't Slow Down. Its title song was a major hit, and the album also yielded Say You, Say Me and Love Will Conquer All.

title: The World Is A Ghetto
label: United Artists Records
personnel: Howard Scott – guitar, percussion, vocals B.B

Harold Brown – drums, vocals Lonnie Jordan – organ, piano, timbales, percussion, vocals Papa Dee Allen – conga, bongos, percussion, vocals Charles Miller – clarinet, alto, tenor and baritone sax, percussion, vocals Lee Oskar – harmonica, percussion, vocals
about: Fifth album by the Long Beach funk band War, released on United Artists in late 1972. It reached number one on the Billboard 200, was Billboard's top-selling album of 1973, and featured The Cisco Kid and the title track.

title: The Band
label: Capitol Records
personnel: Rick Danko – bass guitar, fiddle, trombone, vocals Levon Helm – drums, mandolin, rhythm guitar, vocals Garth Hudson – organ, clavinet, piano, accordion, melodica, soprano, tenor and baritone saxophones, slide trumpet, bass pedals Richard Manuel – piano, drums, baritone saxophone, harmonica, vocals Robbie Robertson – electric and acoustic guitars, engineer

tracks.t: The Night They Drove Old Dixie Down

about: Second album by the Band, recorded largely in a house in Hollywood and often called the Brown Album. Its songs draw on rural American history and include The Night They Drove Old Dixie Down and Up on Cripple Creek.

title: The Payback
label: Polydor
personnel: James Brown - lead vocals, electric piano St
Maceo Parker - alto sax, flute. Darryl "Hasaan" Jamison - trumpet. Jerone "Jasaan" Sanford - trumpet. Isiah "Ike" Oakley - trumpet
Fred Wesley - trombone. Hearlon "Cheese" Martin - guitar
Fred Thomas - bass. John "Jabo" Starks - drums
about: Double album by James Brown originally intended as a film soundtrack before being rejected and released on Polydor. Its long funk grooves topped the R&B album chart, and the title track became a number one R&B single.

title: Aladdin Sane
label: Parlophone
personnel: David Bowie – vocals, guitar, harmonica, sax, synthesiser, mellotron Mick Ronson – guitar, piano, vocals Trevor Bolder – bass. Mick "Woody" Woodmansey – drums
Ken Fordham – sax Brian "Bux" Wilshaw – sax, flutes. Juanita "Honey" Franklin – backing vocals Linda Lewis – backing vocals
about: David Bowie's sixth studio album, largely written during his first American tour as Ziggy Stardust. It became his first UK number one album and is known for its lightning-bolt face cover photograph.

title: Please
label: EMI America
personnel: Neil Tennant – lead vocals and backing vocals, guitars Chris Lowe – synthesizers, programming, sequencers, samplers, computer- generated effects, electric piano, trombone and backing vocals
about: First studio album by the English synth-pop duo Pet Shop Boys, produced by Stephen Hague. It contains the UK number one West End Girls plus Opportunities and Suburbia, and reached the top ten in both Britain and the US.

title: Double Fantasy
label: Geffen Records
personnel: John Lennon – vocals, guitar, piano, keyboards, synthesiser Yoko Ono – vocals Earl Slick, Hugh McCracken – guitar
Tony Levin – bass George Small – keyboards, piano, synthesizer Andy Newmark – drums

tracks.t: Every Man Has A Woman Who Loves Him

about: Joint album by John Lennon and Yoko Ono, recorded in New York and issued on Geffen weeks before Lennon was killed. After his death it went to number one in the US and later won the Grammy for Album of the Year.

title: Hearts
label: Warner Bros. Records
personnel: Gerry Beckley – vocals, guitar, keyboards Dewey Bunnell – vocals, guitar Dan Peek – vocals, guitar, keyboards
about: Fifth studio album by the folk-rock trio America, produced by George Martin. It reached number four in the US and included the chart-topping single Sister Golden Hair as well as Daisy Jane.

title: Workin' Together
label: Liberty Records
personnel: Tina Turner – lead vocals Ike Turner – vocals (intro of "Proud Mary"), all instrumentation The Ikettes – background vocals The Kings of Rhythm – all instrumentation

tracks.t: (As Long As I Can) Get You When I Want You

about: Album by Ike & Tina Turner on Liberty Records, produced by Ike Turner at his Bolic Sound studio. It features their cover of Proud Mary, which became a top five pop hit and won a Grammy.

title: Modern Romans
label: Mercury
personnel: Michael Been – lead vocals, bass, guitar, keyboards Tom Ferrier – guitar, vocals Greg Freeman – bass, vocals Scott Musick – drums, percussion, vocals Steve Huddleston – keyboards, vocals
about: Second album by the California rock band the Call, marked by politically pointed songwriting. Garth Hudson of the Band played keyboards, and the single The Walls Came Down became a modest US hit.

title: Deep In The Heart Of Nowhere
label: Atlantic Records
personnel: Stewart - guitars, keyboards Brian Setzer, Eric Clapton, Jamie West-Oram - guitar Bono, Annie Lennox, Alison Moyet, Maria McKee - guest vocals

tracks.t: Deep In The Heart Of Nowhere

about: First solo studio album by Bob Geldof after his years fronting the Boomtown Rats. Guests include Dave Stewart, Eric Clapton and Annie Lennox, and the lead single was This Is the World Calling.

title: Danger Money
label: Polydor Records
personnel: Eddie Jobson – keyboards, electric violin John Wetton – bass, lead and backing vocals Terry Bozzio – drums, percussion
about: Second and last studio album by the progressive rock group U.K., recorded as a trio of John Wetton, Eddie Jobson and Terry Bozzio. It charted in the US, Canada and the Netherlands.

title: Raising Hell
label: Arista Records
personnel: Joseph "Run" Simmons Darryl "D.M.C." McDaniels Jason "Jam Master Jay" Mizell
about: Third album by the hip hop trio Run-D.M.C., produced by Russell Simmons and Rick Rubin for Profile Records. Its Aerosmith collaboration Walk This Way crossed over to pop radio, and the album became the first hip hop record to go multi-platinum.

title: Sex Machine
label: King Records
personnel: James Brown – vocals, piano. Clayton "Chicken" Gunnels, Darryl "Hassan" Jamison – trumpet. Robert "Chopper" McCollough – tenor sax
Bobby Byrd – organ, vocals. Phelps "Catfish" Collins – guitar. William "Bootsy" Collins – bass

Give It Up Or Turnit A Loose
I Don't Want Nobody To Give Me Nothing
I Can't Stand Myself (When You Touch Me)

about: Double album by James Brown presented as a concert recording, combining live material with studio tracks dressed up with crowd sound. It features early performances by his new band including Bootsy and Catfish Collins.

title: Nothing's Shocking
label: Warner Records
personnel: Perry Farrell – vocals, piano Dave Navarro – electric and acoustic guitars Eric Avery – bass guitar, acoustic guitar Stephen Perkins – drums, percussion
about: First studio album by the Los Angeles alternative rock band Jane's Addiction, released on Warner Bros. Its cover led many retailers to refuse it, yet it was later certified platinum and includes Jane Says.

title: Yield
label: Epic Records
personnel: Eddie Vedder – lead vocals, rhythm guitar Jeff Ament – bass guitar, vocals, photography, layout Stone Gossard – rhythm guitar, vocals, bass Jack Irons – drums, percussion Mike McCready – lead guitar
about: Fifth studio album by Pearl Jam, produced with Brendan O'Brien and noted for its more collaborative songwriting. It debuted at number two in the US and included Given to Fly and Do the Evolution.

title: By The Way
label: Warner Records
personnel: Anthony Kiedis – lead vocals John Frusciante – guitar, vocals, piano, keyboards, synthesizer, Mellotron Flea – bass, guitar Chad Smith – drums, percussion, tambourine
about: Eighth studio album by Red Hot Chili Peppers, produced by Rick Rubin, with a more melodic sound shaped by John Frusciante. It topped the UK chart and included the title track, The Zephyr Song and Can't Stop.

title: To Whom It May Concern
label: Columbia Records
personnel: Andrew Banfield Aaron Brown David Milliner Michael Milliner Hamish Seelochan

tracks.t: Living In The Footsteps Of Another Man

about: First album by the British vocal group the Pasadenas, issued on Columbia. It reached number three in the UK and spawned the hit Tribute (Right On) plus Riding on a Train and Enchanted Lady.
